summary: Claude Hagège is a linguist who studied at several institutions, including under André Martinet in 1971. His career includes posts at the CNRS (~1965–1970), University of Poitiers (1970–1987), EPHE (~1978–1988), and Collège de France (1988–2006).

Claude Jacques was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under George Cœdès (~1961–1969). He served as director at the École française d'Extrême-Orient and taught epigraphy and history at the EPHE (~1970–1999).

Claude Lévi-Strauss was a philosopher who studied at the Paris Law Faculty (~1927–1931) and under Marcel Mauss (~1928–1931). He held posts at the University of São Paulo (~1935–1939), EPHE (~1950–1974), and Collège de France (1959–1982).

Claude-Auguste Court was active in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at the École polytechnique (~1811–1812) and Saint-Cyr (~1812–1813), he served as an engineer officer in the Sikh Khalsa Army and Court of Ranjit Singh (~1827–1843).
Claudia Benthien is a scholar in linguistics who studied at Washington University in St. Louis (1993–1994) and held a post at the University of Hamburg around 2005.
Claudia Weber is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and had her project supervised by Gregor Ahn.
Claudius Buchanan was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Glasgow and Queens' College, Cambridge. In 1801, he served as Vice-Provost of Fort William College.

Claus Oetke was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He taught at Hamburg, Vienna, and Kiel, later heading the Indology department at Stockholm University (1993–2014).

Claus Vogel was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Marburg and Deccan College. He held professorships at the University of Marburg, the University of Göttingen, and served as Ordinarius at the University of Bonn (1976–1998).
Clemency Montelle is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who has held academic posts at the University of Canterbury in 2007 and from 2020 to 2025.

Clinton B. Seely was an Indologist who held an academic post at the University of Chicago, attested in 2007, and later served as Professor Emeritus of South Asian Languages and Civilizations, attested in 2026.

Clyde Kluckhohn was an academic who studied at Princeton, Wisconsin-Madison, Oxford, Vienna, and Harvard. He held positions at the University of New Mexico (~1932–1934) and Harvard University (~1935–1960).

Colette Caillat was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Louis Renou, Jules Bloch, and Walther Schubring. She held posts at the CNRS (~1956–1967), the Sorbonne (1967–1988), and directed the Institut de civilisation indienne (~1967–1990).

Colette Sciberras is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and with traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria.
Colin Mackenzie studied at Dollar Academy and served as the Surveyor General at the Survey of India from 1810 to 1815.
Colin Turnbull was a scholar in Tibetology who completed his studies at Westminster School (~1936–1942), Magdalen College (~1942–1949), and Banaras Hindu University (~1949–1951).

Collett Cox is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned her PhD at Columbia University and studied at Tokyo and Ryukoku. She served as a professor and later Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit at the University of Washington.
Congjun Long is a researcher in computational linguistics and Tibetology who has held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Conor Roddy is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Kathleen Higgins, attested in 2011, and also studied under William Lyons, Arindam Chakrabarti, Graham Parkes, and Roger T. Ames.
